response.sql:
WITH scan_groups AS (
  SELECT
    s.zoneref,
    s.healtheval,
    COUNT(*) as scan_count,
    AVG(
      CASE WHEN sc.gbsize IS NOT NULL AND sc.spanmin IS NOT NULL AND sc.spanmin > 0
        THEN sc.gbsize / sc.spanmin
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ) as avg_ratio
  FROM scans sc
  JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  WHERE sc.chronotag > '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274'
    AND sc.chronotag < '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797'
  GROUP BY s.zoneref, s.healtheval
),
mean_calc AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(avg_ratio) as overall_mean
  FROM scan_groups
),
with_excess AS (
  SELECT
    sg.zoneref,
    sg.healtheval,
    sg.avg_ratio,
    sg.scan_count,
    sg.avg_ratio - m.overall_mean as excess_amount
  FROM scan_groups sg
  CROSS JOIN mean_calc m
  WHERE m.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND sg.avg_ratio > m.overall_mean
)
SELECT
  zoneref,
  healtheval,
  avg_ratio,
  scan_count,
  excess_amount
FROM with_excess
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN excess_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  excess_amount DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: chronotag can be compared as text using standard string comparison operators (> and <) and lexicographic ordering corresponds to chronological ordering. The schema shows text(6) but examples suggest longer storage; actual chronotag format (TIMESTAMP, text-ISO, or numeric Excel serial) is ambiguous.

scan_count includes all scans in each (zoneref, healtheval) group within the time range, even those with NULL gbsize or spanmin. Only scans with both values present and spanmin > 0 contribute to avg_ratio.
Division by zero is prevented by excluding rows where spanmin ≤ 0 from ratio calculation.

alternatives.interpretation: If scan_count should reflect only the scans used in the average calculation (those with valid gbsize/spanmin and spanmin > 0), use COUNT with CASE WHEN instead of COUNT(*), to match the denominator conceptually.
